note: PLACEHOLDER. Every params object here validates against the published district_issue_pulse manifest input_schema (additionalProperties: false, $refs inlined the way publish_experiments.py inlines them), and every value is plausible, but nobody has dispatched one. So a verdict drawn from this list is a claim about the pipeline, not about the agent. EIGHT cases, and DEFAULT_JUDGE_CONFIG.gates.minCases is 20. A corpus verdict over this list therefore resolves CAN'T SAY however the judge voted, because the floor was set from measured agent non-determinism and eight runs measure that rather than the branch. Eight is deliberate and not a rounding error: one clean baseline plus seven single-axis variations is what one change can author honestly across nine agents. Whether to grow every list to 20 or to lower the floor is still open — do not read the shortfall as a decision. Varied along: district population (a Minneapolis ward against a Bellefonte borough ward is two orders of magnitude of voter file rows); urban against rural; and district geometry, which is the shape that decides whether the L2 predicate is a ward string, a bare district number or a whole jurisdiction — City_Ward, City_Council_Commissioner_District, City, County_Commissioner_District and Borough_Ward each appear. How much local news exists to attach to a ranked issue tracks the same axis. People are fictional placeholders in the house style (gp-webapp e2e-tests briefings.spec.ts uses 'Test Official'); this file is public, so no real person is named. States, cities, office titles and L2 voter file column names are real.
